name: COVIDx CT-3
description: Computed tomography (CT) has been widely explored as a COVID-19 screening and assessment tool to complement RT-PCR testing. To assist radiologists with CT-based COVID-19 screening, a number of computer-aided systems have been proposed. However, many proposed systems are built using CT data which is limited in both quantity and diversity. Motivated to support efforts in the development of machine learning-driven screening systems, we introduce COVIDx CT-3, a large-scale multinational benchmark dataset for detection of COVID-19 cases from chest CT images. COVIDx CT-3 includes 431,205 CT slices from 6,068 patients across at least 17 countries, which to the best of our knowledge represents the largest, most diverse dataset of COVID-19 CT images in open-access form. Additionally, we examine the data diversity and potential biases of the COVIDx CT-3 dataset, finding that significant geographic and class imbalances remain despite efforts to curate data from a wide variety of sources.
reputation: One of the largest open-access COVID-19 chest CT datasets; increasingly used in medical imaging research but adoption is moderated by ongoing concerns about label quality and dataset biases.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; large-scale but contains geographic and class imbalances and potential label noise; risk of dataset contamination if used with pretraining data; metrics often also report sensitivity/specificity.
